claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi is an example of the eutectic high-entropy alloy targeted by the hypothesis.
The starting alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar structure containing predominantly FCC regions and a secondary B2, L12, or BCC-related phase.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and undergoes brittle failure.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle failure in the untreated alloy.
Annealing at approximately 500–550 °C for 1–3 hours in an inert atmosphere will promote in situ formation of nanoscale coherent L12 precipitates.
The annealing-induced L12 nanoprecipitates will be finely dispersed in the FCC lamellae.
The L12 nanoprecipitates will form along internal FCC lamellar interfaces.
The coherent L12 nanoprecipitates will act as dislocation sinks.
The coherent L12 nanoprecipitates will act as obstacles that interrupt extended dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Interrupting dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations and delay crack nucleation.
The L12 nanoprecipitates will contribute to strengthening through an Orowan-type mechanism.
The treatment will significantly improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy may exceed 20% tensile elongation.
The treatment will maintain or slightly increase yield and tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy's strength is estimated to remain at or above approximately 900–1074 MPa.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency would diminish the expected ductility and strength improvements.
The magnitude of improvement depends critically on attaining an optimal precipitate size and spatial distribution.
Multicomponent phase-stability effects may interfere with the intended precipitation response during annealing.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows yield strength merely to be maintained, but the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement in yield strength. A result with substantially improved ductility and unchanged strength would satisfy the stated prediction yet be classified as falsifying it.
